title: Broken Retaining Wall
description: A thick limestone retaining wall split across a breached drain bay, with fractured ashlar and a collapse fan.

review.notes: Round 1 of the new budget, judged against the PR #6 round-3 notes. Better: the separate stair is gone, the breach now has a real collapse fan of large blocks, and turf runs along the foot (closeup_base). Still failing: both remnants are still neat stacks of whole rectangular blocks with crisp clean edges; the left remnant steps down evenly on both sides like a stepped pyramid (hero.jpg, closeup_upper). Fix: break the top courses irregularly with fractured block halves and a few blocks displaced or tilted out of plane, so the profile is ragged, not stepped. Rubble infill: it is a grid of small clean cubes in the core of the right remnant, which reads as a voxel pattern, not mortar-bound rubble (closeup_upper). Fix: irregular fist-to-head-size stones set in a darker mortar matrix, recessed behind the facing. The arched niche in the right remnant is unexplained; drop it or make it a drain with a stained outflow. Material: uniform clean white with grey flat-shaded top faces; add weathering at the foot, in the joints and on the top surfaces.
